title: SurrogateModel
description: Model slot, catalog row surrogate-model 1.0.1: the inference contract of the surrogate MLP that emulates the crusher engine, written by data-pipeline/pipeline/stages/train.py to data/derived/models/surrogate.json beside the ONNX graphs data/derived/models/surrogate.onnx (float32) and data/derived/models/surrogate.int8.onnx (dynamically quantised). The input is 11 values: a one-hot of the machine in machine_order, then the continuous inputs in input_order standardised as (value - in_mean) / in_std. The graph's input is named x with shape [1, 11]; its output y has shape [1, 10], standardised: value = y * out_std + out_mean, then 10 ** value where out_log is true, in output_order. Trained on an LHS sweep of the canonical Python engine (pipeline.model.crusher); the held-out metrics are the model-metrics row. The engine itself is the slot's baseline: it answers every query exactly, at a cost the surrogate avoids. Applicability: training.input_ranges is the model's domain; it answers only a point that is not calibrated and inside those ranges, else the engine answers with the reason. Rules the schema cannot state, checked by the producer test: in_mean and in_std have the length of input_order, the out arrays the length of output_order, every std is positive, and the ONNX files named in graphs exist with the sha256 given.

engine_version.description: The product version whose engine produced the training labels.

machine_order.description: The machines in the order of the one-hot that opens the input vector.

input_order.description: The continuous inputs in the order they follow the one-hot.

in_mean.description: The mean of each continuous input on the training draw, in input_order (the input is standardised as (value - in_mean) / in_std).

in_std.description: The standard deviation of each continuous input on the training draw, in input_order.

output_order.description: The outputs in the order of the graph's output vector.

out_log.description: Per output: true when the network predicts its log10 (P80, P50 and P20).

out_mean.description: The mean of each output on the training draw (of its log10 where out_log is true), in output_order (the output is decoded as y * out_std + out_mean).

out_std.description: The standard deviation of each output on the training draw (of the log10 where out_log is true), in output_order.

float32.description: The float32 graph, surrogate.onnx, the one the App runs.

graphs.description: The two exported graphs of the network.

architecture.description: The layer sizes and activations, for example 11-64-64-32-10, SiLU.

seed.description: The seed of the training draw and of torch.

n_train.description: The number of operating points the network was trained on.

n_test.description: The number of points of the independent held-out draw.

sampler.description: How the operating points were drawn, with the bounds per input; the test draw is independent of the training draw.

input_ranges.description: The model's domain: the training range of every continuous input per machine.

torch_version.description: The torch release the network was trained with.

export_parity_max_abs.description: The maximum absolute difference between the trained torch module and the exported float32 graph (run through onnxruntime) on the held-out draw, in standardised output units.

inputRanges.description: The training range of every continuous input, per machine: [low, high] of the training draw, inclusive, written by train.py from sweep.RANGES with no rounding. The applicability rule of both sides reads it: a model answers an operating point only when the point is not calibrated and every continuous input lies inside its machine's range; otherwise the slot's baseline answers, labelled with the reason (calibrated_case, or outside_training_range:<input>).

cone-sec.description: The training ranges of the secondary cone.

cone-tert.description: The training ranges of the tertiary cone.

jaw.description: The training ranges of the jaw crusher.

cone-short-head.description: The training ranges of the short-head cone.

gyratory.description: The training ranges of the gyratory crusher.

ore_axb.description: Ore competence A times b range.

machineRanges.description: [low, high] of every continuous input for one machine.

bytes.description: The size of the graph file [bytes].

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the graph file bytes.

opset.description: The ONNX operator set the graph is exported with.

input.description: The name of the graph's input tensor, x.

output.description: The name of the graph's output tensor, y.

graph.description: One ONNX graph: its file, size, digest, opset and tensor names.
